text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall (oncall-anne): Multiple gateway timeouts and 5xx spikes from runtime cluster eu-west-2 starting ~1779001200. Alert: error-rate=7.8% (5m), avg-latency=2.1s, backlog=digest-queue growth

oncall-anne: I'm on it. grabbing context from traces and routing table.

mike-sre: saw this pop up — scheduler digest backlog growing in the ingest tier, not the model workers yet. suspecting a slowdown in batching flush causing per-request timeouts.

julia-eng: logs from scheduler (snippet):
```
[2026-06-12T18:00:50Z] scheduler.go:458 enqueueDigest id=pool-eu-2 size=11234 latency_ms=450
[2026-06-12T18:01:05Z] batcher.go:212 flushAttempt pool=ingest-eu reason=timeout lastFlush=1200ms
[2026-06-12T18:01:20Z] kvcache.go:87 prefetch miss=0.12 spillover=true
[2026-06-12T18:02:10Z] gateway.go:321 proxy->runtime timeout client=svc-api path=/v1/generate code=504
```

julia-eng: batching flush frequency seems off — flushes are getting pushed later as queue grows. could be GC pauses on scheduler hosts or disk pressure on batching journal.

yana-pm: Customer impact: Support reports 6 distinct customers with failures impacting production flows (payments webhook retries, chat UI timeouts). CS ticket IDs: #C-4721, #C-4723. Frontend shows 504s intermittently.

support-ops: Confirming — we have 18 customer-facing errors in the last 10m, top customers affected: AcmeCorp, Shoply. SLA hit: partial degradation. Notifying accounts.

oncall-anne: quick checks i'll run now: 1) `kubectl get pods -n runtime -l app=scheduler` 2) check disk i/o and GC on scheduler nodes 3) scaling policies for batching pool 4) reroute policy to fallback route if latency >1.5s

mike-sre: run `kubectl top pods -n runtime | grep scheduler` and `ps aux | grep -i scheduler` if you need process-level CPU spikes. also check `iostat -x 1 3` on node.

oncall-anne: results: cpu on schedulers normal ~40%. iostat shows avgqu-sz spiking to 8 on node-i-07 (high io wait). `dmesg` shows repeated read stalls. also one scheduler pod OOMKilled around 1779001500 and restarted.

julia-eng: that OOM restart would explain the backlog growth — recovered but backlog kept growing during restart window. need to prevent HOL-style blocking where digest for a stalled pool blocks newer requests.

alex-ml: side note: some requests include very long prompt chains increasing KV cache pressure; not ideal during congestion. we can enable prefix-pruning in runtime temporarily: `RUNTIME_PREFIX_PRUNE=true` to limit kv size.

oncall-anne: mitigation plan proposed: 1) enable fallback route to lower-capacity models for non-critical routes 2) increase scheduler pod replicas by 2 in eu-west-2 3) apply temporary rate-limit on bulk ingest endpoints 4) restart node-i-07 after cordon and drain if io wait persists

ops-bot: @channel scheduled action: `kubectl scale deploy/scheduler -n runtime --replicas=6` initiated by oncall-anne at 1779001605.

julia-eng: I'll push a small change to batching config to reduce max-batch-delay from 1.2s to 600ms to favor latency over batch size (short-term). patch: `config.batch.max_delay_ms=600`

mike-sre: be careful — reducing delay will increase token cost but should immediately lower 5xx by avoiding head-blocking large digest frames.

oncall-anne: executed scaling. new pod count 6, pods coming up. also applied rate-limit for `/v1/ingest/bulk` to 50 rps.

support-ops: CS update: customers notified of degraded performance, they asked for ETA. what's our ETA for visible improvement?

oncall-anne: expecting improvement within 2-4 minutes after scaling and reduced batch delay. will update when error-rate drops below 1%.

(2 minutes later)

ops-bot: metric update: error-rate=3.2% (now), avg-latency=1.4s, digest-queue-size=4300

julia-eng: good trend. we need to investigate root cause: one scheduler node had IO contention probably due to journal compaction — open follow-up for infra to review disk health and journald retention.

alex-ml: temporary KV pruning helped. if we re-enable full prompts later, recommend a model-level timeout guard to cap extreme token lengths.

mike-sre: postmortem action items (quick list):
- infra: replace/repair disk on node-i-07, confirm io subsystem
- runtime: add graceful digest eviction / per-pool digest timeouts to avoid single-pool stalls
- routing: add automated fallback policy when digest-queue grows >5k for 3m
- cost/product: evaluate impact of lower batch delay on unit cost and adjust autoscale rules

yana-pm: noted. i'll coordinate customer follow-ups and send a summary to affected accounts.

support-ops: errors trending down to 0.7% — I'll update tickets and mark as partial-resolved.

oncall-anne: leaving note in incident tracker: `INC-2026-233-scheduler-digest-backlog` with timeline, mitigation commands, and next steps. handing back to oncall rotation in 30m.

incident-bot: Incident marked as "mitigated" by oncall-anne at 1779002760.

mike-sre: fine to close after infra confirms disk/OS fix and we push runtime eviction logic.

julia-eng: will open an RFC for digest eviction and a small runtime patch for adaptive batch delay.

yana-pm: thanks everyone for the quick coordinated response.

support-ops: :thumbsup:
